record.original_question: Does every closed Lorentzian manifold have at least one closed geodesic?

evidence.quote: Does every closed Lorentzian manifold have at least one closed geodesic?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A Lorentzian manifold is a smooth manifold $M$ equipped with a smooth, non-degenerate symmetric (0,2)-tensor field $g$ of signature $(-,+,+,\dots,+)$. A geodesic is an inextendible smooth curve $\gamma:I\to M$ satisfying $\nabla_{\dot\gamma}\dot\gamma = 0$, where $\nabla$ is the Levi-Civita connection of $g$; the geodesic is called closed if there exists $T>0$ such that $\gamma(t+T)=\gamma(t)$ and $\dot\gamma(t+T)=\dot\gamma(t)$ for all $t$ (equivalently, it factors through a non-trivial smooth periodic curve $S^1\to M$).

Question: Does every closed (i.e., compact and without boundary) Lorentzian manifold $(M,g)$ admit at least one closed geodesic?
artifact.status_search_result: The question has been answered in the negative. Recent work (Mehidi–Zeghib, "On closed geodesics in Lorentz manifolds", GAFA 2024) constructs compact Lorentzian manifolds (e.g., quotients of SL(2,R) or Sol with suitable left-invariant Lorentzian metrics) that possess no closed geodesics whatsoever. Thus, in contrast to the Riemannian case, not every closed Lorentzian manifold admits a closed geodesic. (In dimension 2 every compact Lorentzian surface still has a definite closed geodesic, and in the homogeneous setting closed geodesics always exist.)

status_evidence.title: On Closed Geodesics in Lorentz Manifolds (GAFA)
status_evidence.snippet: Constructs compact Lorentz manifolds, namely certain quotients of SL(2,R) or Sol with left-invariant Lorentzian metrics, having no closed geodesics.
status_evidence.claim: There exist closed Lorentzian manifolds with no closed geodesic, settling the question negatively in general.

status_evidence.title: On closed geodesics in Lorentz manifolds (arXiv)
status_evidence.snippet: We construct compact Lorentz manifolds without closed geodesics; in dimension 2 every compact Lorentzian surface admits a definite closed geodesic.
status_evidence.claim: Counterexamples exist in dimension ≥ 3, while compact Lorentzian surfaces always have closed geodesics.

status_evidence.title: Open problems and questions about geodesics — Burns & Matveev
status_evidence.snippet: Lists the existence of closed geodesics on compact Lorentzian manifolds as an open problem at the time of writing.
status_evidence.claim: The problem was historically posed as open before the recent counterexamples.
